tldr: Headlines across 12 of 13 country-buckets converge on a single security claim — Iran tried to assassinate one of Netanyahu's sons — rendered with near-identical phrasing across four languages. Iraq alone rejects the threat-frame entirely, contextualising the Israel-Iran war as Netanyahu's long-sought strategic objective whose payoff now looks uncertain.

single_outlet_findings.finding: One Le Parisien headline (idx 12) is entirely off-topic — covering Trump's proposed $100,000 US tech visa — and entered the cluster via feed proximity rather than story relevance. The second Le Parisien headline (idx 13) anchors the ECONOMIC frame on Iran's economic collapse under US sanctions.

The only outlet to reject the assassination-claim frame entirely. The headline reframes the war as Netanyahu's long-sought strategic objective while questioning whether it achieved his desired outcome — a retrospective political assessment absent from every other title in the corpus.

Uses 'Makes Massive Claim' — the only English-language headline to introduce explicit epistemic skepticism about Netanyahu's statement, signalling political rather than purely security framing. All other outlets report the claim neutrally ('says', 'reveals') or use distancing quotes ('claims').

bottom_line: The headline layer presents this story almost universally as a live security-threat narrative — Iran targeting Netanyahu's family — while suppressing the electoral timing context (an October election imminent) that body-text coverage foregrounds.
